Messages.Author: Lönkka
Messages.Body:
> theEmperor wrote:
> I misread the rules, effects targeting allies cant be used so I assume you can't use it, still curious about blood to water though.
>
From the "Rules" PDF's FAQ:
Q: Can I burn an Adversary with Entombment/Blood of Sandman/etc.?
A: No, as Adversaries are immune to card effects which target allies.

While Blood to Water isn't specifically mentioned, it still is a card that targets Allies so by default it is not playable just in the same way Entombement isn't playable.

I think the idea probably was to force people to brutally pound the adversaries instead of cheesily disposing them with clever tricks.

The rules as announced don't prohibit Imbued. 75% of the vampires in your crypt must be of the same clan. But it doesn't say that 75% of your crypt must be the same clan. So with 12 Imbued in your crypt, 75% of the 0 vampires you have must be the same clan.

Caitiff are screwed except for the 25% option, yes.

>
I'm pretty certain that playing an Imbued deck where 9 of your Imbued had to be the same creed would be awful.

> Joscha wrote:
> Because they have just three of each creed? Scarce clans do also.
>
Pretty different problem. They're (mostly) designed to be used singly(*), so a deck with three of one Scarce vampire and 9 helpers from another clan wouldn't be impossible, or adding a Nagaraja to a Necromancy deck or something. Yeah, it kinda sucks that you can't easily play a star vampire deck with 5 copies of a scarce vampire and a bunch of off-clan helpers, or really stand a chance of championing the True Brujah in most of these 75% storylines, but all sorts of decks are restricted in storylines. (One of the more annoying being that - assuming a 12 card crypt - you can have only three copies of Anarch Convert, and quite a few people play 4 or 5 of them ordinarily.) Maybe if you could find a good way of turning one of them into a turbo-deck...

(*) According to playtesters, an early version of the Scarce rule was that all Scarce vampires contested each other, rather than the penalty we currently have. So presumably at least the initial design was no two Salubri ever being used by the same Methuselah - and possibly, as a consequence, no likelihood of even including two different Salubri in the same crypt. Probably some corner-case trickery where you might prefer one Salubri over the other mid-game, but not generally so.
